solutionSource.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

entries.clue: Speaker in court upset judge (6)

indicatorNotes.upset: something upset is knocked over, so the word for judge is turned round

blocks.note: to court someone is to woo them; 'in' ties the fragment on
REF, the referee who judges a match, turned over

annotation.surface: A witness in a courtroom is thrown by an irritated judge.
annotation.walkthrough: The courtroom scene makes 'court' a law court and 'Speaker' a person on the stand; both are traps, since the speaker is a loudspeaker and court means romance.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by example: a hi-fi loudspeaker cabinet holds several drivers, and this one reproduces the deep bass notes.

entries.clue: Humpty Dumpty figure, typically round and hollow (5)

blocks.note: the letter O is round
void = empty, hollow

annotation.surface: A description of the nursery-rhyme egg: round and empty inside.
annotation.walkthrough: Humpty Dumpty is traditionally drawn as an egg, and 'typically' flags that his shape is one example of the answer.
annotation.definitionFit: The word means egg-shaped, from Latin ovum, and nursery-rhyme illustrations always draw Humpty as an egg.

entries.clue: Briefed about retaining least depleted feature of sewage works (6,3)

indicatorNotes.about: letters knocked about are scattered, so BRIEFED is rearranged
indicatorNotes.retaining: the rearranged word keeps LT held inside its letters
indicatorNotes.depleted: something depleted has been drained, so LEAST loses its inner letters

blocks.note: anagram fodder, taken as printed
LEAST with EAS removed
anagram indicator

annotation.surface: Someone was briefed on the least-worn-out part of a sewage plant.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Briefed' looks like it must be replaced by a synonym, but it is used letter for letter as the fodder.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by example: treatment plants trickle waste water through tanks of gravel or sand to clean it, one of several stages.

entries.clue: Verses of short song, cutting about Starmer primarily (6)

indicatorNotes.short: a word cut short loses its tail, so HYMN drops the N
indicatorNotes.cutting: something cutting another splits it, so HYM goes between R and E
indicatorNotes.primarily: primarily means first of all, so only the opening letter of Starmer counts

blocks.note: re = about, concerning; HYM goes between its letters
HYMN with its last letter off
first letter of Starmer

annotation.surface: A political jingle about Keir Starmer, the UK prime minister, is being cut down.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Cutting' reads as satire aimed at Starmer, but it is a placement instruction; Keir Starmer is the Labour prime minister of the UK.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: short poems, such as nursery pieces or limericks, are called by this word as well as verses.

entries.clue: Hiss and abuse boxing team across Belgium (8)

indicatorNotes.boxing: to box something in is to enclose it, so SLATE wraps round the rest
indicatorNotes.across: lying across something straddles it, so the team's two letters sit either side of B

blocks.note: to slate = to criticise harshly; its S and LATE wrap round the middle
a football or cricket team is 11, written here as two ones
B is Belgium's international vehicle code

annotation.surface: Someone hisses and hurls insults at a sports team playing in Belgium.
annotation.walkthrough: Crossword teams are usually XI; here the number 11 is written with two ones, which is the step most solvers miss.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonym, from Latin sibilare: the verb means producing a sustained s-sound, as snakes and whisperers do.

entries.clue: Nothing whatsoever in a few nasty names roughly embodying Democrat? (5,5,5)

indicatorNotes.roughly: done roughly means not done precisely, so the letters come out of order
indicatorNotes.embodying: to embody something is to take it into your body, so the letters hold D inside

blocks.note: anagram fodder, 14 letters
D = Democrat
anagram indicator

annotation.surface: A US Democrat is being called a few rude names.
annotation.walkthrough: The phrase, often shortened to 'sweet FA', is British slang; it began as Navy slang for tinned meat.
annotation.definitionFit: British idiom: the phrase, a polite stand-in for a ruder expression, means absolutely nothing, as in 'we got sweet FA for it'.

entries.clue: Time Bill lifted hearts in place where Robin drinks? (8)

indicatorNotes.lifted: in a down answer, lifting a word raises its bottom to the top, so TAB reads upward

blocks.note: bird is British slang for time in prison, as in 'doing bird'
TAB, a bill in a bar, turned upside down
H = hearts, the card suit

annotation.surface: A man called Bill steals hearts in a pub where his friend Robin drinks.
annotation.walkthrough: Robin looks like a man's name heading for a drink; the capital hides the bird, and the question mark admits the robin is only one example.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by example: a garden basin of water serves robins and other small birds for drinking and washing.

entries.clue: Pressure group left flyer, hard to ignore (5)

indicatorNotes.to ignore: anything ignored is left out, so the H for hard is dropped from HOBBY

blocks.note: L = left
HOBBY, a small falcon, without H for hard

annotation.surface: A campaign group has left a leaflet that is hard to ignore.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Flyer' reads as a leaflet in the campaigning surface, but here it is the hobby, a small falcon.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: organised interests that try to sway politicians were named after the parliamentary hall where they buttonholed members.

entries.clue: Chance to work with elite, no frills specialist (9)

indicatorNotes.to work: letters set to work are put through their paces, so CHANCE and LIT are rearranged
indicatorNotes.no frills: frills are trimmings at the edge, so ELITE loses its first and last letters

blocks.note: anagram fodder, taken as printed
ELITE without its first and last E
anagram indicator

annotation.surface: A job offer to work with top people, in a no-frills setting.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Chance' is used as printed rather than swapped for a synonym, and 'no frills' reads as budget rather than as trimming.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonym, both adjectives: jargon or knowledge belonging to one expert field is described with either word.

entries.clue: Insect Australian sheep tolerate (6,4)

blocks.note: woolly is Australian slang for a sheep
to bear = to tolerate

annotation.surface: An Australian sheep puts up with an insect.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Australian' makes you look for a country or an abbreviation, but it names the slang: in Australia a sheep can be called a woolly.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by example: the hairy caterpillar of the tiger moth goes by this name, and a larva still counts as an insect.

entries.clue: Rugby player struck ultimately by taxi travelling west (4)

indicatorNotes.ultimately: ultimately means in the end, so only the final letter of struck is used
indicatorNotes.travelling west: an across entry reads eastward, so heading west means reading right to left

blocks.note: last letter of struck
a cab is a taxi; K is set next to it, then the whole K CAB turns round

annotation.surface: A rugby player is hit by a taxi heading west.
annotation.walkthrough: The accident scene makes 'struck by taxi' one idea, but 'by' only puts K beside CAB before the pair is reversed.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by example: in rugby the players stationed behind the scrum, such as wingers and full-backs, are collectively called by this name.

entries.clue: Supporter of approach where very little is changed for that woman (8)

indicatorNotes.where: where points into the approach word, marking it as the place the change happens
indicatorNotes.is changed for: something changed for another is swapped out, so V gives way to HER

blocks.note: an advent is an arrival, an approach
V = very, and it is only one letter
her = that woman

annotation.surface: A backer of a policy under which a tiny amount is swapped for a woman.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Very little' describes a single letter: V, the abbreviation for very, is what gets replaced.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: someone who sticks to a cause or leader, from Latin adhaerere, to cling, is a follower or backer.

entries.clue: US singer missing extremely creative day in past (6)

indicatorNotes.missing: a missing piece is absent, so the singer's name goes without the letters that follow
indicatorNotes.extremely: the extremes of a word are its ends, so only C and E of creative are taken

blocks.note: BEYONCE without CE, the ends of creative
D = day

annotation.surface: An American singer who lost her creative spark on some day in the past.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Day in past' reads as one phrase, but 'in' is a link: the definition is just 'past', as in 'past the station'.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonym, both prepositions: further than a point, as in 'the house past the church' or 'beyond the church'.

entries.clue: Youngster defending Student Union (4)

indicatorNotes.defending: a defender surrounds what it protects, so CUB goes round L

blocks.note: a cub is a young animal, or a young scout; it opens to take L
L = learner, a student

annotation.surface: A young person stands up for the students' union.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Student Union' looks like one institution; it splits, with Student giving L and Union the definition.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: an association of members joined by a shared interest, such as a golf or book society.

entries.clue: Rock ace not “semi-literate”, revolutionary claims (9)

indicatorNotes.revolutionary: a revolution turns something right round, so the hidden letters read upward
indicatorNotes.claims: to claim something is to take hold of it, so the phrase holds the answer inside

blocks.note: acE NOT SEMI-Literate, to be read backwards

annotation.surface: A rock-star ace insists he is not semi-literate, and a revolutionary makes claims.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Rock ace' reads as a guitar hero, and the quotation marks make 'semi-literate' look like the thing to decode, but the letters simply run backwards through the phrase.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by example: a sedimentary stone formed mainly of calcium carbonate, used for building and cement.

entries.clue: Object found in transport café, traditionally on the counter (8)

indicatorNotes.found in: something found in a place is inside it, so the answer lies within the phrase
indicatorNotes.on the counter: counter means running against, so the letters are read against the usual direction

blocks.note: transporT CAFÉ, TRAditionally, to be read backwards

annotation.surface: Something left on the counter of a roadside café, as is the custom.
annotation.walkthrough: The café scene makes 'counter' the thing you order at; here it means going against the reading direction. A transport café is a cheap British roadside diner for lorry drivers.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: a man-made item, especially one of historical interest dug up by archaeologists, is called this.

entries.clue: Spooner’s curious electrical device that’s used in the kitchen (6,3)

annotation.definitionNote: a descriptive phrase: 'something that's used in the kitchen'

indicatorNotes.Spooner’s: the Reverend Spooner was famous for swapping the opening sounds of words

blocks.note: prying = nosy, curious
an electric fan
swap the P and F sounds

annotation.surface: An odd electric gadget found in someone's kitchen.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Electrical device that's used in the kitchen' looks like the definition of a blender; the device is only the fan, and the kitchen item is not electric at all.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by description: a shallow long-handled pan for cooking eggs and bacon on the hob is a kitchen staple.

entries.clue: Bull, perhaps, from present US president (8)

blocks.note: present = here, as in a register
Gerald Ford, 38th US president

annotation.surface: A gift of a bull from the current American president.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Present US president' reads as whoever is in office now; present is split off as HERE, and the president is Ford.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by example: a red-and-white English breed of beef cattle, so a bull may belong to it; 'perhaps' marks the example.

entries.clue: A little dog is with men on manoeuvres (8)

indicatorNotes.on manoeuvres: troops on manoeuvres move about in the field, so the letters shift position

blocks.note: anagram fodder
anagram fodder, joined by 'with'
anagram indicator

annotation.surface: A small dog accompanies soldiers on an army exercise.
annotation.walkthrough: 'A little dog' reads as a puppy; 'A little' is the definition and 'dog' is fodder.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: a tiny amount, as in 'just a smidgen of milk'; this spelling is a less common variant.

entries.clue: Daughter departs put off about Connecticut college (4)

indicatorNotes.departs: someone who departs leaves, so the D for daughter leaves DELAY
indicatorNotes.about: about can mean turned round, as in about-face, so the letters reverse

blocks.note: D = daughter, the letter to remove from DELAY
DELAY = put off, without its D

annotation.surface: A daughter leaves, having postponed news about her Connecticut college.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Put off' reads as discouraged, but it means postponed, DELAY.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by example: an Ivy League university in New Haven, founded in 1701.

entries.clue: Root striking ball matching Pope’s last run (6)

indicatorNotes.striking: striking can mean striking out, deleting, so the ball-shaped O is removed
indicatorNotes.last: the last of a word is its final letter, so only the end of Pope is used

blocks.note: GOING, as in colours going together, with O struck out
last letter of Pope
R = run, in cricket scoring

annotation.surface: Joe Root, the England batter, hits the ball in time with Pope's final run.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface is cricket: Joe Root and Ollie Pope bat for England. The ball is the round letter O, struck out of GOING.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by example: the spicy underground rhizome of Zingiber, sold in shops as a knobbly root.

entries.clue: Mind whisper principal murmured (6)

indicatorNotes.murmured: a murmur is spoken softly, so only the sound of the words counts

blocks.note: a sigh is a whisper of breath; key = principal, as in key figure

annotation.surface: An instruction to whisper something to the head teacher.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Principal' reads as a school head, but it is the adjective: key.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonym, from Greek for breath or soul: psychologists use it for the whole human mental self.

entries.clue: Cycle bent round tree (5)

indicatorNotes.Cycle: a cycle goes round and round, so the front letters of ARCED move to the back

blocks.note: bent into a round shape = arced; AR then moves to the end
cycling indicator

annotation.surface: A bicycle, its frame bent, wrapped round a tree after a crash.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Cycle' looks like a bike in the crash scene; it tells you to rotate the letters.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by example: a tall coniferous evergreen of Lebanon and the Himalayas, prized for fragrant timber.

entries.clue: Diamond, say, extra pay at intervals secures, reversing transfer (8)

indicatorNotes.at intervals: things spaced at intervals have gaps between them, so every other letter is taken
indicatorNotes.secures: to secure something is to hold it fast, so the alternate letters hold NEIL inside
indicatorNotes.reversing: reversing goes backwards, so the whole assembled string is turned round

blocks.note: ExTrA pAy, every other letter; NEIL goes before the final A
Neil Diamond, the American singer

annotation.surface: An odd payroll instruction: a diamond or a bonus is secured, then the transfer is reversed.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Diamond, say' looks like a gem, a pitch or a card; it is Neil Diamond, whose name reads backwards in the middle of the answer.
annotation.definitionFit: Legal sense: handing ownership of property to someone else is to alienate it, which is why rights can be inalienable.

entries.clue: Military volunteers once getting letter from Crete? (5)

blocks.note: split 3-1-1: the article plus the initials of Britain's former part-time reserve army
a character of the Greek alphabet, as used on the island

annotation.surface: Old army volunteers receive a letter posted from Crete.
annotation.walkthrough: Split three-one-one, the answer is the Territorial Army, Britain's volunteer reserve until it became the Army Reserve in 2014. The question mark admits the letter is from the Greek alphabet, not the post.
annotation.definitionFit: Two senses: the eighth Greek alphabet character, used on Crete, and the article plus the abbreviation of Britain's former part-time army.

entries.clue: Become very angry leaving automatic essentially in “Drive” (4)

indicatorNotes.leaving: a letter leaving a phrase walks out of it, so M is taken out of GO MAD
indicatorNotes.essentially: the essence of a word is its core, so the middle letter of automatic is meant

blocks.note: to go mad is to become very angry; GO is the first part
MAD = very angry, less its M
middle letter of autoMatic, M, which is removed

annotation.surface: A driver loses their temper over the automatic gearbox's Drive setting.
annotation.walkthrough: The quotation marks around 'Drive' make it the gear selector's D; it is the definition, meaning to urge on.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonym, both verbs: a goad was originally a pointed stick for prodding cattle forward, so to push or spur someone on.

entries.clue: Limits wearing old DJ and possibly tangerine jacket (6,4)

indicatorNotes.wearing: a word wearing another has it put on, so RANGE takes O in front of it

blocks.note: O = old
the range of something is its limits
John Peel, the long-serving BBC radio DJ

annotation.surface: An old DJ's taste stretches as far as a tangerine-coloured jacket.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Tangerine jacket' reads as a loud piece of clothing; the jacket is the fruit's skin, and 'possibly' marks a tangerine as one kind of orange.
annotation.definitionFit: Playful description: the skin wrapped round a citrus fruit is its jacket, and a tangerine is one variety of that fruit.

entries.clue: Wanting golf game, ambassador succeeded to tour islands (8)

indicatorNotes.Wanting: wanting means lacking, so the card game is missing its G for golf
indicatorNotes.to tour: touring a place means going all round it, so HE and S surround BRIDE

blocks.note: HE = His or Her Excellency, an ambassador's title
BRIDGE, the card game, minus G, golf in the phonetic alphabet
S = succeeded

annotation.surface: An ambassador who wanted a round of golf got to tour some islands instead.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Golf game' reads as a round on the course; golf is just the letter G, taken from the card game bridge.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by example: the Inner and Outer groups off Scotland's west coast, including Skye and Lewis, share this name.

entries.clue: Catwalk model wary around Quant occasionally (6)

indicatorNotes.model: to model clay is to reshape it, so the letters are reshaped
indicatorNotes.around: WARY sits around UN before the reshaping
indicatorNotes.occasionally: something done occasionally happens now and then, so every other letter of Quant is taken

blocks.note: anagram fodder, as printed
qUaNt, every other letter
anagram indicator

annotation.surface: A catwalk model is nervous around the designer Mary Quant.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Model' reads as the person on the catwalk; it is a verb telling you to reshape the letters. Mary Quant was the British designer behind the miniskirt.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonym, chiefly American: the raised strip that fashion models parade along during a show.
